maturation_deltas: MI creates very strong live evidence for cross-carrier recovery/diversion, air-group reorganization, layered search/recontact, fast surface pursuit and repeat torpedo attack. These are experience/organizational triggers; later institutional maturation must still be dated rather than retroactively assumed.
Hornet inspection and captured Midway equipment create a small learning input for Japanese radar/CIC/base/damage-control study; no immediate performance multiplier is applied.
dependency_notes: All legacy 81/82/85/86/87+ summer-autumn outcome lines are blocked until rerun from this checkpoint.
Repair and personnel clocks are projections, not already-completed state.

territory.Midway: Japanese-held as of about 1942-06-15; heavily damaged and not yet a mature base

United_States.Pacific_fast_carrier_state: temporary zero before Wasp transfer; Ranger remains Atlantic unless strategic emergency forces reconsideration
United_States.aircrew_note: Hull losses are much larger than personnel losses; many experienced carrier aviators/deck/support personnel survive for later Essex/CVL force generation.

role_priority: force US Hawaii defense and interdiction expenditure
midway_base_policy.garrison_center: about 4500-6000 after consolidation, subject to logistics review
midway_base_policy.initial_air_center: A6M about 24-36, recon/seaplane about 10-20, land bombers about 12-18 as forward/rotational force; H6K/H8K detachments as conditions permit
midway_base_policy.sustainment_policy: Exploit the short US carrier gap to build initial 2-3 month stockpile, then reduce regular lift and accept a submarine-interdiction tax rather than over-garrison.

allied_interdiction.immediate: No near-term carrier-backed recapture. US submarines and Hawaii-based air/recon become primary pressure tools.
allied_interdiction.japanese_ASW_effect: Focused priority convoys are harder to reattack and suffer fewer avoidable formation/escort failures, but first-shot submarine opportunity is not eliminated.
allied_interdiction.working_summer_cost: For Midway sustainment specifically, use about 15-25% extra ship-days/escort-days/route-delay burden as a working range; direct transport/auxiliary losses about 1-3 over three summer months plus damaged ships is a provisional center, not yet a closed ledger.

repair_rebuild_projection.Shokaku: return roughly late June if yard/air-group checks close
repair_rebuild_projection.Hiryu: hull/flight-deck repair roughly late July-August; combat return after air-group work-up
repair_rebuild_projection.Japanese_carrier_airgroups: 8-12 week serious rebuild/reorganization window is favored; surviving experts are not to be fed immediately into a Guadalcanal-style attrition cycle unless a new emergency forces it.

Japan: No historical post-Midway panic conversion program. Continue Hiyo/Ryuho/Taiho/Unryu-family paths; retain long-term dedicated fast-carrier quantity demand.
Do not automatically convert Ise/Hyuga or Chitose/Chiyoda immediately solely because of MI.
Raise priority of escorts, oilers, repair/salvage capacity and standardized transports because PM/Solomons/Midway create long simultaneous sustainment tails.
United_States: Existing Essex and Independence programs become top fleet priority; avoid design changes that delay hull completion.
Wasp transfers to Pacific; Ranger remains Atlantic unless Hawaii emergency overrides European/Atlantic need.
Preserve surviving carrier aviators, deck crews, fighter-direction and damage-control personnel to seed new Essex/CVL groups.
Near-term fleet doctrine places more weight on radar surface screens, night-pursuit avoidance, damaged-carrier escape and submarine/land-air attrition while carrier numbers are low.
Britain: Operation C loss of Indomitable/Formidable remains a major fleet-carrier deficit; European/Med commitments likely pull scarce modern decks west, leaving Indian Ocean weak and emphasizing CVE/light-carrier acceleration and conversion studies.
